newsitem.title: UK: Three polls show dip in support for UK's Labour.
newsitem.headline: Three polls show dip in support for UK's Labour.

text.p: The British opposition Labour Party's opinion poll lead ahead of May 1 elections dipped sharply in two opinion polls published in Sunday newspapers and was stuck at a comparatively narrow 16 points in a third.

A Gallup poll in the Sunday Telegraph gave Labour a 16 point lead over Prime Minister John Major's Conservative Party, down seven points from a week ago. It was the narrowest lead for Labour since Tony Blair became its leader three years ago.
An ICM poll in the Observer also put Labour 16 points ahead of the Conservatives, but this was unchanged from the previous week.
And an NOP poll for the Sunday Times, gave Labour a 20-point lead, down four points from last week.
Gallup showed support for Labour at 49 percent, the Conservaties at 33 percent and the Liberal Democrats at 12 percent.
ICM gave Labour 48 percent and the Conservatives 32 percent, down one point from last week, while the Liberal Democrats were up one point at 15 percent.
The NOP poll also showed the Liberal Democrats gaining against Labour, showing them up five points to 17 percent, their best NOP rating since May 1996.
Labour was at 48 percent and the Conservatives were unchanged at 28 percent.
The polls followed an apparent policy switch by Labour when it announced last week that it now favoured privatisation of some state assets provided this was in the public interest.
The NOP poll showed 33 percent of voters opposed Labour's new position on privatisation while 22 percent supported it.
However, 55 percent of voters were in favour of more privatisations -- which have been one of the key features of the Conservatives' 18 years in power.
